notes.text: Samuel Langhorne Clemens, known by the pen name Mark Twain, was an American writer, humorist, and essayist.
Mark Twain's novels include The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) and its sequel, Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884), with the latter often called the "Great American Novel".
Mark Twain also wrote A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court (1889) and Pudd'nhead Wilson (1894) and cowrote The Gilded Age: A Tale of Today (1873) with Charles Dudley Warner.
Mark Twain is remembered as a writer connected with United States.
Mark Twain's recorded life dates place this profile around 1835-1910.
